title: Acts Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who sold a possession in Acts 5?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1 states that a certain man named Ananias sold a possession.

questions.question: What did Ananias and Sapphira do with part of the price from the sale?
options: Gave it all to the apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 5:2 explains that Ananias kept back part of the price of the land.

questions.question: What did Peter accuse Ananias of lying to?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:3 indicates that Peter asked Ananias why he lied to the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: True or False: Ananias fell down and died after Peter spoke to him.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:5 mentions that Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost after hearing Peter's words.

questions.question: What happened to Ananias after he died?
options: He was buried by the young men
He was left on the ground
He was taken to the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: He was buried by the young men
questions.explanation: Acts 5:6 states that young men arose, wound him up, and buried him.

questions.question: How long after Ananias's death did Sapphira come in?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:7 specifies that Sapphira came in about the space of three hours after Ananias.

questions.question: True or False: Sapphira knew what had happened to her husband when she entered.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:7 indicates that Sapphira came in not knowing what was done.

questions.question: What did Peter ask Sapphira about the sale of the land?
options: If she sold it for less
If she sold it for so much
If she kept back part of it
questions.correctAnswer: If she sold it for so much
questions.explanation: Acts 5:8 shows Peter asking Sapphira if they sold the land for so much.

questions.question: What did Sapphira answer to Peter's question?
options: No, we sold it for less
questions.explanation: Acts 5:8 records Sapphira saying 'Yea, for so much' in response to Peter.

questions.question: True or False: Sapphira also fell down and died after speaking to Peter.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:10 states that Sapphira fell down straightway at Peter's feet and yielded up the ghost.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the church after these events?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:11 indicates that great fear came upon all the church after these events.

questions.question: In Acts 5, who performed many signs and wonders?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:12 states that by the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought.

questions.question: What did the people do to the sick in Acts 5?
options: Brought them to the high priest
questions.explanation: Acts 5:15 mentions that they brought forth the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and couches.

questions.question: What did the angel of the Lord tell the apostles after their imprisonment?
options: To go and speak in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: To go and speak in the temple
questions.explanation: Acts 5:20 records that the angel instructed the apostles to go, stand and speak in the temple.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the apostles do that resulted in many signs and wonders being wrought among the people?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:12 indicates that many signs and wonders were done by the apostles when they were all in one accord, emphasizing the importance of unity in the church.

questions.question: What did the high priest and those with him feel towards the apostles?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:17 states that the high priest and those with him were filled with indignation, showing their anger towards the apostles' actions.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were immediately released from prison without any divine intervention.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:19 reveals that the angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, indicating divine intervention was necessary for their release.

questions.question: What were the apostles instructed to do after being freed from prison?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:20 commands the apostles to stand and speak in the temple, highlighting their mission to continue preaching despite opposition.

questions.question: How did the council react when they discovered the apostles were teaching in the temple?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:28 indicates that the high priest confronted the apostles for continuing to teach, showing their anger and frustration.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were afraid of the people and did not preach in the temple.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:21 shows that the apostles entered the temple early in the morning to preach, demonstrating their boldness despite potential danger.

questions.question: What was the response of the apostles when questioned by the high priest?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:29 shows that Peter and the apostles stated they ought to obey God rather than men, affirming their commitment to divine authority.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:32 reveal about the apostles' relationship with the Holy Ghost?
options: They were filled with the Holy Ghost
They did not mention the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: They were filled with the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 5:32 indicates that the apostles are witnesses of the things of God, along with the Holy Ghost, whom God gives to those who obey Him.

questions.question: What principle does Acts 5:39 teach about opposing God's work?
options: It will succeed if it is of men
It cannot be overthrown if it is of God
questions.correctAnswer: It cannot be overthrown if it is of God
questions.explanation: Acts 5:39 emphasizes that if the work is from God, it cannot be overthrown, warning against fighting against divine purposes.

questions.question: What did Gamaliel advise the council regarding the apostles?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:38 records Gamaliel's advice to refrain from the apostles, suggesting that if their work is of God, it will prevail regardless.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were beaten but rejoiced for suffering shame for Jesus' name.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:41 states the apostles rejoiced after being beaten, demonstrating their faith and willingness to suffer for Christ.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the apostles' teaching after their release?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:42 confirms that the apostles did not cease to teach and preach Jesus Christ, showing their commitment to their mission.

questions.question: How does Acts 5:25 demonstrate the persistence of the apostles despite opposition?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:25 illustrates that the apostles were found teaching in the temple after being imprisoned, showing their unwavering dedication.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who were the two individuals that conspired to keep back part of the price of the land they sold?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1 states that a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession.

questions.question: What was Peter's accusation against Ananias regarding his lie?
options: He lied to the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: He lied to the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: In Acts 5:3, Peter says, 'Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost...?' indicating that the lie was directed at the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What happened to Ananias after he was confronted by Peter?
options: He fell down and gave up the ghost
questions.correctAnswer: He fell down and gave up the ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 5:5 records that 'Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost.'

questions.question: What did Peter tell Sapphira when she came to him?
options: Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?
questions.correctAnswer: Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:8 shows Peter asking Sapphira, 'Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?' as a direct confrontation about her involvement.

questions.question: How did the apostles respond to the command not to teach in Jesus' name?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:42 states that 'daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ,' showing their commitment to obey God over men.

questions.question: What significant theme does Acts 5:29 highlight regarding obedience?
options: Obey the laws of the land
questions.explanation: Acts 5:29 captures the apostles' declaration, 'We ought to obey God rather than men,' emphasizing their priority of divine authority.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:31 say about Jesus' status after His resurrection?
options: He is a Prince and a Saviour
questions.correctAnswer: He is a Prince and a Saviour
questions.explanation: Acts 5:31 declares that Jesus is exalted as 'a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.'

questions.question: Which historical figure did Gamaliel mention when advising caution toward the apostles?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:36 mentions Theudas, who rose up and attracted followers, which Gamaliel used as an example to caution the council.

questions.question: According to Acts 5:39, what is the consequence of opposing God's work?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:39 states, 'But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God,' indicating futility in opposing divine work.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the phrase 'we ought to obey God rather than men'?
questions.explanation: The statement represents parallelism as it contrasts two commands, emphasizing the priority of obedience to God over human authority.

questions.question: True or False: Ananias and Sapphira were punished for lying about their donation.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:5 and Acts 5:10 confirm that both Ananias and Sapphira fell down dead after lying about their donation, indicating punishment.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were afraid to preach after being imprisoned.
questions.explanation: Acts 5:42 shows that the apostles continued to teach and preach Jesus Christ despite being warned not to, demonstrating their fearlessness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet's message of repentance is echoed in Acts 5:31?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's messages often emphasized repentance and forgiveness (Ezekiel 18:30), which resonates with Acts 5:31's theme of repentance given through Jesus.

questions.question: What Greek word related to power is used in Acts 5:39 regarding God's work?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'dunamis' refers to power, implying that if the work is of God, it possesses divine power that cannot be overthrown.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:3 imply about the nature of Ananias' sin?
options: He lied to the Holy Ghost
He sold his land for too little
questions.correctAnswer: He lied to the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 5:3 states, 'But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost...' indicating that Ananias' primary sin was lying to God rather than merely financial wrongdoing.

questions.question: According to Acts 5:11, what was the reaction of the church after the events with Ananias and Sapphira?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:11 describes that 'great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things,' showing the seriousness of the situation and its impact on the community.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Acts 5:4 regarding ownership?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:4 highlights that the land was Ananias' own, and after it was sold, it remained under his control. This exemplifies God's sovereignty over ownership and resources.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 5:30-31 teach regarding Jesus?
options: Jesus is a Prince and Saviour
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is a Prince and Saviour
questions.explanation: Acts 5:31 declares, 'Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour,' affirming Jesus' divine authority and role in salvation.

questions.question: What significant event followed the apostles' imprisonment, as described in Acts 5:19?
options: They were released by the high priest
An angel opened the prison doors
They were set free by the governor
questions.correctAnswer: An angel opened the prison doors
questions.explanation: Acts 5:19 states, 'But the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth,' demonstrating divine intervention in their ministry.

questions.question: In Acts 5:29, what principle do Peter and the apostles affirm?
options: We ought to obey God rather than men
questions.correctAnswer: We ought to obey God rather than men
questions.explanation: Acts 5:29 records Peter and the apostles stating, 'We ought to obey God rather than men,' emphasizing the primacy of divine authority over human commands.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:42 reveal about the apostles' commitment after their release?
options: They ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: They ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 5:42 indicates that the apostles continued their mission 'daily in the temple, and in every house,' reflecting their unwavering commitment to the Gospel.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Acts 5:36-39 convey about human efforts against divine plans?
options: If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it
questions.correctAnswer: If it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it
questions.explanation: Acts 5:39 states, 'But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God,' emphasizing that God's purposes prevail despite human opposition.

questions.question: What does the narrative of Ananias and Sapphira teach about sin and accountability, as seen in Acts 5:4?
options: You have not lied unto men, but unto God
questions.correctAnswer: You have not lied unto men, but unto God
questions.explanation: Acts 5:4 emphasizes the seriousness of lying to God, indicating that accountability for sin extends beyond human authority to divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Acts 5:12 contribute to the understanding of the apostles' authority?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:12 states, 'And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people,' showing that their authority was confirmed through miraculous acts.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:25 demonstrate about the apostles' influence in Jerusalem?
options: They filled Jerusalem with their doctrine
questions.correctAnswer: They filled Jerusalem with their doctrine
questions.explanation: Acts 5:28 indicates that the apostles had spread their teaching widely, leading to significant influence in Jerusalem during that time.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:6 indicate about the aftermath of Ananias' death?
options: He was brought back to life
questions.explanation: Acts 5:6 mentions that 'the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him,' indicating a swift and discreet burial following his death.

questions.question: What does Acts 5:40 reveal about the council's response to the apostles?
options: They commanded them to stop speaking in Jesus' name
questions.correctAnswer: They commanded them to stop speaking in Jesus' name
questions.explanation: Acts 5:40 shows the council's attempt to suppress the apostles' message by commanding them not to speak in Jesus' name, reflecting their opposition to the Gospel.

questions.question: How does Acts 5:17-18 reflect the Sadducees' attitude towards the apostles?
questions.explanation: Acts 5:17 states that the high priest and the Sadducees were filled with indignation, showing their antagonism towards the apostles and their teachings.

questions.question: What does the mention of Gamaliel in Acts 5:34 suggest about wisdom in the council?
options: He was a respected voice of reason
questions.correctAnswer: He was a respected voice of reason
questions.explanation: Acts 5:34 highlights Gamaliel's reputation as a Pharisee and a doctor of the law, suggesting that he provided a wise perspective amidst the council's anger.
